K1806.author: Daniel J. Galvin
K1806.note: Stronger penalties can deter wage theft; the structure of the policy and its enforcement matter.
K1806.design: observational: original dataset of state laws, new estimates of minimum-wage violations, difference-in-differences on a dozen state wage-theft laws

K1807.title: Theory and Evidence on Employer Collusion in the Franchise Sector
K1807.author: Alan B. Krueger, Orley Ashenfelter
K1807.publisher: Journal of Human Resources 57(S):S324-S348 (NBER Working Paper 24831, 2018)
K1807.note: No-poaching-of-workers clauses in 58 percent of major franchisors' contracts (2016); more common in low-wage, high-turnover industries.
K1807.design: descriptive analysis of 2016 Franchise Disclosure Documents, with theory

K1808.title: First DOJ Criminal Wage-Fixing and No-Poach Trials End in Acquittals
K1808.author: Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati
K1808.note: U.S. v. DaVita Inc. and Kent Thiry (D. Colo.): not guilty on all counts, Apr 15, 2022. U.S. v. Neeraj Jindal and John Rodgers (E.D. Tex.): not guilty of conspiracy, Apr 14, 2022; Jindal convicted on one obstruction count. Replace with DOJ or court records when retrieved.

K1809.title: Positive Health Externalities of Mandating Paid Sick Leave
K1809.author: Stefan Pichler, Katherine Wen, Nicolas R. Ziebarth
K1809.publisher: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management 40(3):715-743 (IZA Discussion Paper 13530, 2020)
K1809.note: Doctor-certified influenza-like-illness rates fell about 11 percent (290 cases per 100,000 patients per week) in the first year after sick-pay mandates.
K1809.design: quasi-experimental: difference-in-differences on administrative state-week data, 2010-2018

K1810.title: Randomized Government Safety Inspections Reduce Worker Injuries with No Detectable Job Loss
K1810.author: David I. Levine, Michael W. Toffel, Matthew S. Johnson
K1810.note: 9.4 percent decline in injury rates and 26 percent reduction in injury costs; no evidence of losses in employment, sales, credit ratings or firm survival.
K1810.design: natural experiment: 409 randomly inspected California establishments compared with 409 matched controls

K1811.title: Why Do Sectoral Employment Programs Work? Lessons from WorkAdvance
K1811.author: Lawrence F. Katz, Jonathan Roth, Richard Hendra, Kelsey Schaberg
K1811.publisher: Journal of Labor Economics (NBER Working Paper 28248)
K1811.note: Sector-focused programs for low-wage workers produce substantial and persistent earnings gains of 11 to 40 percent after training completion.
K1811.design: synthesis of randomized evaluations of sectoral training programs

K1812.title: An Effectiveness Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis of Registered Apprenticeship in 10 States
K1812.author: Debbie Reed, Albert Yung-Hsu Liu, Rebecca Kleinman, Annalisa Mastri, Davin Reed, Samina Sattar, Jessica Ziegler
K1812.publisher: Mathematica Policy Research for U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
K1812.note: Participants had substantially higher earnings than nonparticipants; social benefits much larger than costs.
K1812.design: nonexperimental comparison of participants with nonparticipants
K1812.interest: contractor report for the agency that runs the program

K1813.title: Economics of Estate Taxation: A Brief Review of Theory and Evidence
K1813.author: Wojciech Kopczuk
K1813.publisher: Tax Law Review 63(1):139-157 (NBER Working Paper 15741, Feb 2010)
K1813.note: Audit-based avoidance estimates of 8 to 13 percent of liability; valuation discounts on about 6 percent of returns averaging about 10 percent of gross estate; estate restructuring in the last months of life and death-date responses to reforms.

K1815.title: Universal Baby Bonds Reduce Black-White Wealth Inequality, Progressively Raise Net Worth of All Young Adults
K1815.author: Naomi Zewde
K1815.note: Median young-adult white to Black wealth ratio about 16:1 without baby bonds and 1.4:1 with them.
K1815.design: microsimulation on Panel Study of Income Dynamics data; no behavioral response assumed

K1816.title: Shared Capitalism at Work: Employee Ownership, Profit and Gain Sharing, and Broad-based Stock Options
K1816.author: Douglas L. Kruse, Richard B. Freeman, Joseph R. Blasi (eds.)
K1816.publisher: University of Chicago Press for NBER
K1816.note: Covers prevalence, free-rider and risk problems, firm performance and worker outcomes, including a chapter on risk and lack of diversification.
K1816.interest: academic; editors study and support broad-based ownership

K1817.title: How Did Employee Ownership Firms Weather the Last Two Recessions? Employee Ownership, Employment Stability, and Firm Survival, 1999-2011
K1817.author: Fidan Ana Kurtulus, Douglas L. Kruse
K1817.publisher: W.E. Upjohn Institute for Employment Research
K1817.note: Employee owners reported fewer layoffs (GSS 2002: 3.0 vs 9.2 percent; 2010: 2.6 vs 12.3 percent); prior studies find higher survival and steadier employment; correlational.
K1817.design: observational: Form 5500 pension records matched to Compustat, 1999-2011; survival models; GSS survey comparisons

K1819.title: Recession Ready: Fiscal Policies to Stabilize the American Economy
K1819.author: Heather Boushey, Ryan Nunn, Jay Shambaugh (eds.)
K1819.publisher: The Hamilton Project and Washington Center for Equitable Growth
K1819.note: Chapter 3 (Sahm) proposes automatic direct payments tied to unemployment-rate changes; Chapter 6 (Chodorow-Reich and Coglianese) proposes UI trigger changes. The landing page names Nunn and Shambaugh as editors.

K1820.title: Family Options Study: 3-Year Impacts of Housing and Services Interventions for Homeless Families
K1820.author: Daniel Gubits, Marybeth Shinn, Michelle Wood, Stephen Bell, Samuel Dastrup, Claudia D. Solari, Scott R. Brown, Debi McInnis, Tom McCall, Utsav Kattel
K1820.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (Abt Associates; Vanderbilt University)
K1820.note: Long-term subsidy (voucher) arm: less than half as many later homelessness episodes; child separations reduced at 20 months, not detected at 37 months; better housing stability and food security; modest earnings reductions narrowed.
K1820.design: randomized trial: 2,282 families assigned to four arms

K1821.title: How Do Changes in Housing Voucher Design Affect Rent and Neighborhood Quality?
K1821.author: Robert Collinson, Peter Ganong
K1821.note: Metro-wide increases in voucher generosity raised rents with minimal change in unit or neighborhood quality; rent ceilings indexed to neighborhood rents moved holders to lower-crime, lower-poverty areas.
K1821.design: quasi-experimental analysis of two voucher policy changes

K1822.title: The Effects of Legal Representation on Tenant Outcomes in Housing Court: Evidence from New York City's Universal Access Program
K1822.author: Michael T. Cassidy, Janet Currie
K1822.publisher: Journal of Public Economics (article 104844); NBER Working Paper 29836 (2022)
K1822.note: Tenants who gained lawyers were less likely to receive possessory judgments, be evicted or have warrants issued, and faced smaller money judgments.
K1822.design: quasi-experimental: program rollout with address-level housing court data, 2016-2019

K1824.title: The Role of Behavioral Frictions in Health Insurance Marketplace Enrollment and Risk: Evidence from a Field Experiment
K1824.author: Richard Domurat, Isaac Menashe, Wesley Yin
K1824.note: Deadline reminders raised enrollment 1.3 percentage points (16 percent); average spending risk fell 5.1 percent; marginal enrollees 37 percent less costly. Auto-enrollment was not tested.
K1824.design: randomized field experiment: mailed information to 87,000 households in California's marketplace

K1825.title: Estimated Budgetary Effects of Public Law 117-169, to Provide for Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of S. Con. Res. 14
K1825.author: Congressional Budget Office
K1825.note: Sec. 11001 (drug price negotiation; 11002-11003 included) reduces outlays by $98.521 billion over 2022-2031.

K1826.title: Supporting Community College Students from Start to Degree Completion: Long-Term Evidence from a Randomized Trial of CUNY's ASAP
K1826.author: Michael J. Weiss, Alyssa Ratledge, Colleen Sommo, Himani Gupta
K1826.note: 18 percentage point effect on 3-year graduation; 10 percentage points on 6-year graduation.

K1827.title: Closing the Gap: The Effect of Reducing Complexity and Uncertainty in College Pricing on the Choices of Low-Income Students
K1827.author: Susan Dynarski, C.J. Libassi, Katherine Michelmore, Stephanie Owen
K1827.note: Application rose from 26 to 68 percent and enrollment from 12 to 27 percent; no new aid was added.
K1827.design: randomized experiment: early guarantee of free tuition at a flagship university

K1828.title: Creating Moves to Opportunity: Experimental Evidence on Barriers to Neighborhood Choice
K1828.author: Peter Bergman, Raj Chetty, Stefanie DeLuca, Nathaniel Hendren, Lawrence F. Katz, Christopher Palmer
K1828.note: Treatment raised the share moving to high-upward-mobility areas from 15 to 53 percent, driven mainly by customized search assistance.
K1828.design: randomized trial with housing voucher recipients, plus a second trial and qualitative interviews

K1829.title: Local Economic Development, Agglomeration Economies, and the Big Push: 100 Years of Evidence from the Tennessee Valley Authority
K1829.author: Patrick Kline, Enrico Moretti
K1829.publisher: Quarterly Journal of Economics (NBER Working Paper 19293)
K1829.note: Agricultural gains reversed after subsidies ended; manufacturing gains kept growing; aggregate income in the TVA region rose for an extended period; regional agglomeration gains offset by losses elsewhere.
K1829.design: long-run comparison of TVA and comparison counties with a spatial equilibrium model

K1830.title: The Benefits and Costs of the Clean Air Act from 1990 to 2020 (Second Prospective Study)
K1830.author: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air and Radiation
K1830.note: Central benefits estimate exceeds costs by more than 30 to 1.

K1831.title: What Caused Racial Disparities in Particulate Exposure to Fall? New Evidence from the Clean Air Act and Satellite-Based Measures of Air Quality
K1831.author: Janet Currie, John Voorheis, Reed Walker
K1831.note: The Clean Air Act accounts for over 60 percent of the Black-white convergence in PM2.5 exposure since 2000.
K1831.design: quasi-experimental: Clean Air Act regulation with satellite-based PM2.5 measures

K1832.title: The Opportunity Atlas
K1832.author: Raj Chetty, John N. Friedman, Nathaniel Hendren, Maggie R. Jones, Sonya R. Porter (companion paper, NBER Working Paper 25147)
K1832.publisher: Opportunity Insights and U.S. Census Bureau
K1832.note: Public atlas of mean adult outcomes by childhood Census tract built with confidential Census data under Census disclosure review.
K1832.design: administrative data on adult outcomes by childhood census tract
K1832.interest: academic research group with the Census Bureau

K1833.title: The contact hypothesis re-evaluated
K1833.author: Elizabeth Levy Paluck, Seth A. Green, Donald P. Green
K1833.note: Contact typically reduces prejudice (pooled 0.39, Glass's delta); weaker effects for racial and ethnic prejudice; no studies of adults' racial or ethnic prejudice; few longitudinal studies.
K1833.design: meta-analysis of 27 randomized studies with outcomes measured at least one day later

K1835.title: Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015 (anaw 2)
K1835.author: National Assembly for Wales
K1835.note: Well-being duty on public bodies, well-being goals, Future Generations Commissioner, public services boards. Says nothing about evaluation.

K1836.title: Equilibrium Effects of Pay Transparency
K1836.author: Zoe B. Cullen, Bobak Pakzad-Hurson
K1836.note: Laws lead wages to decline by approximately 2 percent overall, with smaller effects where workers have little individual bargaining power.
K1836.design: model plus empirical analysis of US state laws protecting the right to discuss pay

K1839.title: Does Disability Insurance Receipt Discourage Work? Using Examiner Assignment to Estimate Causal Effects of SSDI Receipt
K1839.author: Nicole Maestas, Kathleen J. Mullen, Alexander Strand
K1839.note: For the roughly 23 percent of applicants on the margin, employment would have been 28 percentage points higher without benefits; near zero for severe impairments, up to 50 points for less severe.
K1839.design: instrumental variables using disability examiners' allowance rates

K1841.title: American Indian Self-Determination: The Political Economy of a Policy that Works
K1841.author: Stephen Cornell, Joseph P. Kalt
K1841.publisher: Harvard Kennedy School Faculty Research Working Paper RWP10-043
K1841.note: States that self-determination is the only policy that has made significant progress against distressed conditions in Native communities. No outcome estimates on the landing page.
K1841.design: political-economy analysis of congressional sponsorship of legislation since 1970, with review
K1841.interest: academic research program on Native nation development

K1842.title: The Role and Design of Net Wealth Taxes in the OECD
K1842.author: OECD
K1842.note: Covers current and historical use of net wealth taxes in OECD countries.
